bibliographic.abstract: Non-polar magnetic nanoparticles agglomerate upon cooling. This process is followed by in-situ small angle X-ray scattering to assess structural properties of the emerging agglomerates. On the length scale of a few particle diameters, no differences are found between the agglomerates of small ( d = 12nm) and large ( d = 22nm) nanoparticles. Hard-sphere like random packing with a local packing fraction of η = 0 . 4 is seen. On larger length scales, small particle form compact superstructures, while large particles arrange into agglomerates that resemble chain-like structure in SAXS. This can be explained by directed magnetic dipole interactions that dominate larger particles, while isotropic van der Waals interaction governs the agglomeration of smaller particles.

samples.sample_description: Spherical iron oxide nanoparticles with d ≈ 10 nm; core diameter 11.8 nm and PDIcore 0.11.
samples.sample_state: dispersion in chloroform was stabilised by an oleic acid shell of roughly 2 nm thickness

samples.sample_description: Spherical iron oxide nanoparticles with d ≈ 20 nm; core diameter 21.5 nm and PDIcore 0.11.
samples.sample_state: dispersion in chloroform was stabilised by an oleic acid shell of roughly 2 nm thickness

datasets.dataset_name: Magnetic hysteresis loops at room temperature
datasets.dataset_description: The magnetic moments were measured by a vibrating sample magnetometer using magnetic hysteresis loops at room temperature.

datasets.dataset_name: Small Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS) at room temperature
datasets.dataset_description: Small-angle scattering curves of FeNP10 and FeNP20 at 293 K to determine precise size distributions and ensure the absence of any agglomerates.

datasets.dataset_name: Temperature dependent Small Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS)
datasets.dataset_description: Temperature dependent measurements ranging between 153 K and 293 K were performed on samples in borosilicate capillaries; scattering curves were recorded every 10 K for decreasing temperature.
